phase3_findings.description: The blank-string coercion accepts an empty or whitespace-only value for save_text_memories and reads it as off, while the sibling booleans exposed through the same MCPB ${user_config.<bool>} mapping (MemoryConfig.save_queries, allow_import, allow_admin_tools, DatabaseConfig.read_only) have no such coercion and raise a validation error at startup instead. The final pass adds the related case of a bundle upgraded from a version predating the field, where an unreplaced ${user_config.save_text_memories} placeholder blocks server startup rather than reading as off. No decided criterion asks for either behavior.

The internal docs claim the prompt's section numbered 2. TEXT MEMORY is not printed when the flag is off, repeated at docs/internal/setup/config-loading.md line 30, but the new assertions in tests/unit/test_factory_wiring.py lines 483, 498 and 513 match only the bare text TEXT MEMORY, so the section-number half of the claim has no test behind it. The claim itself holds against src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py.

The new eight-line comment names the wrong change and its consequence only in its last three lines; the first five restate what save_text_memory is for and how has_text_memory gates the prompt section, which docs/internal/agent/memory.md already records. The comment is accurate. Reported in the previous iteration with no decision recorded and still present at this head.

The pre-existing save_queries comment still says dropping the registration drops the prompt guidance with it, which is the claim this change corrects for the text-memory case in docs/internal/agent/memory.md line 96 and docs/internal/setup/config-loading.md line 30, because the save sentence rides on has_search and survives. The diff mirrors the corrected wording into the new comment but leaves this sibling comment unchanged. The line is outside the diff and is an internal code comment, so it is a clarity gap only.

## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (four suggestions, none blocking)

This pull request is ready to merge: every one of the fifty-one checklist claims passed, all five decided acceptance criteria are itemized and met by the shipped code, and the four remaining findings are suggestions about wording and consistency that change no behavior.

Rule applied: rule 6 — a finding below the threshold remains → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)

<details><summary>4 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 218 to 227 accept a blank or whitespace-only value for `save_text_memories` and read it as off, but the sibling boolean settings exposed the same way do not. `mcpb/manifest.json` maps `SQLLENS_DATABASE__READ_ONLY` and the new `SQLLENS_MEMORY__SAVE_TEXT_MEMORIES` through the same `${user_config.<bool>}` substitution, while `MemoryConfig.save_queries`, `allow_import`, `allow_admin_tools` and `DatabaseConfig.read_only` have no such coercion and would raise a validation error at startup instead. One reviewer adds the related case of a bundle upgraded from a version that predates the field, where an unreplaced `${user_config.save_text_memories}` placeholder would stop the server from starting rather than read as off; that trigger is speculative and the failure is loud. No decided criterion asks for either behavior. (raised by 2/3 agents)
2. The claim in `docs/internal/agent/memory.md` line 112, repeated in `docs/internal/setup/config-loading.md` line 30, is that with the flag off the prompt's `2. TEXT MEMORY` section is not printed, including the section number. The new tests in `tests/unit/test_factory_wiring.py` at lines 483, 498 and 513 assert only on the bare text `TEXT MEMORY`, so the numbering half of that claim has no test behind it. The claim itself holds against `src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py`. (raised by 1/3 agents)
3. The comment at `src/sqllens/agent/factory.py` lines 132 to 139 runs eight lines, and only the last three name the wrong change and its consequence, which is not to move the gate into `SaveTextMemoryTool.execute` or `ChromaAgentMemory.save_text_memory` because that would drop curated notes. The first five lines restate what `save_text_memory` is for and how `has_text_memory` gates the prompt section, which `docs/internal/agent/memory.md` already records. The comment is accurate. This was reported in the previous iteration and no decision was recorded against it. (raised by 1/3 agents)
4. The pre-existing comment at `src/sqllens/agent/factory.py` lines 121 to 123 still says that dropping the `save_queries` registration drops the prompt guidance with it. That is the very claim this change corrects for the text-memory case in `docs/internal/agent/memory.md` line 96 and `docs/internal/setup/config-loading.md` line 30, because the save sentence rides on `has_search` and survives. The diff mirrors the corrected wording into the new comment but leaves this sibling comment unchanged. The line is outside the diff and is an internal code comment, so this is a clarity gap only. (raised by 1/3 agents)

</details>
